items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I had some nice French musicians with me such as Eddie Louis, Guy Peterson, etc.

ctx.x: In February 1968, I was elected a member of the French Academy du Jazz. The function of the Academy du Jazz is to pick the best jazz records issued during the year and give it an award. There were distinctions for different categories, Blues, New Orleans, Modern Jazz, Singers, etc. We would also elect the best French musician of the year. A well known foreign musician who has been the European scene for years, the trumpetist Arthur Briggs, and an American named Sim Coppans, who had a jazz programme on radio for…

In May, Jeff Gilson asked me if I would accept to record an album of Negro Spirituals for a guy named Pou-Dubois who owned a studio. We recorded some well known spirituals and some which were completely unknown. Jeff made the arrangements. We made a contract stipulating that I would get royalties when Pou-Dubois would sell the tape and the record would be issued. We recorded the 8/9/11th of May, 1968. I had some nice French musicians with me such as Eddie Louis, Guy Peterson, etc.

But Pou-Dubois didn't sell the tape to a record company. He made a transaction with the International Guild du Disque in Switzerland, without stipulating that I was supposed to receive royalties. In fact, he signed a statement declaring that all the musicians and artists had been paid and had no right to claim payment or royalties. So I couldn't get any money from the Guild and it was not worthwhile to sue Pou-Dubois at the moment as he was not solvent, according to some people.
